sentences.en: It's only relatively recently that designers have become aware of the need to be inclusive when designing products.
sentences.zh: 设计师们直到最近才开始意识到，在设计产品时需要具备包容性。

sentences.en: But what does that mean exactly?
sentences.zh: 但这究竟意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, it simply means designing products that span economic, social and cultural barriers.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，它指的是设计能够跨越经济、社会和文化障碍的产品。

sentences.en: It means making sure products are accessible, so that as man: y different types of people as possible can use them, without any type of adaptation having to be made to the original design.
sentences.zh: 这意味着确保产品具有可及性，从而使尽可能多的不同类型人群都能使用它们，而无需对原始设计进行任何调整。

sentences.en: Inclusive design is often linked with universal design, although they are not quite the same thing.
sentences.zh: 包容性设计常与通用设计相关联，尽管二者并不完全相同。

sentences.en: Universal design aims to make products that work for everyone and that includes considering the needs of people who have cognitive difficulties, which can present quite a challenge.
sentences.zh: 通用设计旨在打造适用于所有人的产品，其中包括考虑认知障碍人士的需求，而这往往颇具挑战性。

sentences.en: Today examples of successful inclusive design can be seen all around us.
sentences.zh: 如今，成功的包容性设计实例随处可见。

sentences.en: In workplaces it is common to see desks which can be adjusted to suit people of different heights or for wheelchair users This still isn't always the case, however, and is one reason why office workers often suffer from back or neck problems.
sentences.zh: 在工作场所，我们常见可调节高度的办公桌，以适应不同身高的人群或轮椅使用者。然而，目前这种情况尚未普及，这也是办公室工作人员常患背部或颈部问题的原因之一。

sentences.en: You'll find another example in the public toilets of countless hotels, airports and offices.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子可见于众多酒店、机场和办公楼的公共卫生间。

sentences.en: Taps that you activate by sensor require no pressing or twisting movements.
sentences.zh: 通过传感器启动的水龙头无需按压或旋转操作。

sentences.en: These are not only more hygienic, they're also easier for people with dexterity or mobility issues.
sentences.zh: 这类水龙头不仅更加卫生，也更便于手部灵巧性或行动能力受限者使用。

sentences.en: The tech industry has been criticised in the past for focusing too much on young consumers, but this is changing.
sentences.zh: 科技行业过去曾因过于关注年轻消费者而受到批评，但这一状况正在改变。

sentences.en: Man: y products are now designed with the elderly in mind.
sentences.zh: 如今许多产品在设计之初便已将老年人纳入考量。

sentences.en: For example, it's well known that vision declines with age and that we also become worse at distinguishing between similar colours, in particular shades of blue, which is why software designers rarely create interfaces with this colour.
sentences.zh: 例如，众所周知，视力会随年龄增长而衰退，且我们辨别相似颜色（尤其是各种蓝色色调）的能力也会下降，因此软件设计师极少采用蓝色来设计用户界面。

sentences.en: Motor skills also decline with age and some people have difficulty doing everyday things like picking up a cup or opening a door.
sentences.zh: 运动技能同样会随年龄增长而退化，一些人甚至难以完成诸如端起杯子或开门等日常动作。

sentences.en: This can also affect their ability to use a mouse or keyboard.
sentences.zh: 这还可能影响他们使用鼠标或键盘的能力。

sentences.en: So voice access is now a routine way of making commands.
sentences.zh: 因此，语音访问如今已成为下达指令的一种常规方式。

sentences.en: It's worth looking at the problems non -inclusive designs cause when not enough consideration is given to a range of users, as it can have a serious impact on people's lives.
sentences.zh: 值得审视的是，当设计缺乏包容性、未能充分考虑各类用户需求时所引发的问题，因为这可能对人们的生活造成严重影响。

sentences.en: Access is one obvious example because it has such a huge impact on disabled people's independence.
sentences.zh: 无障碍通行就是一个显而易见的例子，因为它对残障人士的独立性具有巨大影响。

sentences.en: Not being able to access public transport because buses or trains are not wheelchair means man: y disabled people can go out unless someone goes with them.
sentences.zh: 由于公交车或火车不具备轮椅无障碍设施，导致许多残障人士无法独自乘坐公共交通出行，除非有人陪同。

sentences.en: Safety is another issue.
sentences.zh: 安全是另一个问题。

sentences.en: Inexplicably, most cars are still crash-tested using a dummy based on an average -sized male.
sentences.zh: 令人费解的是，目前大多数汽车仍使用基于平均体型男性假人的碰撞测试。

sentences.en: This has safety implications for all women, particularly those who are pregnant, as the seatbelts worn by the dummy are not adapted to accommodate them.
sentences.zh: 这对所有女性（尤其是孕妇）的安全都构成影响，因为假人所佩戴的安全带并未针对她们的身体特征进行适配。

sentences.en: Over the past 100 years, workplaces in the UK have, on the whole, become considerably safer.
sentences.zh: 在过去100年中，英国的工作场所总体上已变得安全得多。

sentences.en: Employers are legally required to provide well-maintained personal protective equipment, or PPE, anything from goggles to full bodysuits, to workers who need it, free of charge.
sentences.zh: 雇主依法必须免费向有需要的员工提供保养良好的个人防护装备（PPE），范围从护目镜到全身防护服不等。

sentences.en: But most PPE is designed to fit men.
sentences.zh: 但大多数个人防护装备都是按男性体型设计的。

sentences.en: A recent report found that employers often think that when it comes to female workers, all they need to do to comply with this legal requirement is to buy jackets, for example, designed for a small man.
sentences.zh: 一份最新报告发现，雇主往往认为，只要为女性员工采购例如专为体型较小男性设计的夹克，就已满足此项法律要求。

sentences.en: The problem with this is that women can be tall and still have much smaller shoulders than the average man.
sentences.zh: 这种做法的问题在于：女性可能身高很高，但肩宽却远小于男性平均水平。

sentences.en: Ill -fitting PPE such as high -vis jackets, vests and body armour can put women at risk.
sentences.zh: 不合身的个人防护装备——例如高可视性夹克、背心和防弹衣——会使女性面临风险。

sentences.en: The report found that 95% of women said that their PPE often hampered their work and that this problem was worst in the emergency services. particularly the police.
sentences.zh: 该报告发现，95%的女性表示其个人防护装备经常妨碍工作，而这一问题在应急服务机构（尤其是警察部门）中最为严重。

sentences.en: Another problem is related to comfort at work.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题与工作时的舒适度有关。

sentences.en: A very common scenario in offices in summertime is to see women wrapped in blankets or wearing sweaters while the air conditioning is on high.
sentences.zh: 夏季办公室里一种非常常见的场景是：空调开得很足，而女性却裹着毛毯或穿着毛衣。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the men are in shorts and T -shirts.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，男性则穿着短裤和T恤。

sentences.en: This is due to differences in metabolic rates for men and women.
sentences.zh: 这源于男女基础代谢率的差异。

sentences.en: There is a standard setting for air conditioning to be at a temperature of 21 degrees designed to suit men and in most modern offices it is not possible to turn the air conditioning up or down.
sentences.zh: 空调温度的标准设定为21摄氏度，旨在适应男性需求；而在大多数现代办公场所，无法调节空调温度。

sentences.en: This means that man: y offices which mainly employ women are wasting energy by having the air conditioning set too high.
sentences.zh: 这意味着主要雇用女性的办公室因空调温度设定过高而白白浪费能源。

sentences.en: As you can see from the examples I've just mentioned, there are serious consequences for designs which don't consider the needs of all users.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所举的例子所示，忽视全体用户需求的设计会带来严重后果。
